challenges.title: Login card
challenges.brief: I'd like you to build the sign-in page for Fernway, our project planning app. The people landing here are returning customers who just want to get back to work, so signing in should take seconds and nothing on the page should compete with the form. Keep it calm and warm, in line with the rest of Fernway. All the wording is supplied, and the attached reference is exactly what we want: match it as closely as you can. It needs to work with a keyboard and a screen reader. It's done when a returning customer can sign in, reset a forgotten password or find their way to creating an account without having to think about it.

A white card with a thin border and rounded corners, centred on a warm off-white page
The brand line is small, bold, uppercase and green; the heading is the largest text on the card
Each input is tied to its label, and Sign in is a real button inside a form

challenges.title: Footer with columns
challenges.brief: Our marketing site for Harbor stops abruptly, and I need you to give it a proper ending. Visitors who scroll this far are interested, so give them one last confident nudge to start a trial, then a footer that helps anyone looking for something specific find it quickly: product pages, company information, help and the legal bits. You have all the copy, and the reference design is the target; the closer your page gets to it, the better. Keep it tidy and quiet so the nudge stands out. It's done when a visitor can either start a trial or find any link they need within a few seconds.

challenges.title: Nav bar with hero
challenges.brief: Northwind needs the first screen of its homepage, the part every visitor sees before they decide whether to stay. In a few seconds they should know what Northwind is, why it helps their team, and what to do next, with one main action clearly ahead of the alternative. Give them a simple way to move around the site as well, and make sure our new feature announcement gets noticed. The copy is supplied, and the attached reference shows the finished screen exactly, so match it as closely as you can. It's done when a first-time visitor can explain what we do and knows exactly where to click to get started.

challenges.title: Blog post header
challenges.brief: We're redesigning the article pages on our design blog, and I want you to start with the opening of a post: the part that convinces someone to keep reading. Use our current feature as the example; the text is supplied, and the reference design is precisely what we want this to look like. It should read like a thoughtful magazine, not a tech blog, with the title doing the real work and the author information easy to find without crowding it. Readers must be able to tell what the piece is about and how long it will take before they scroll. It's done when it reads like a page you'd want to finish.

challenges.title: Pricing with three plans

All the plan details are supplied, and the attached reference is the page we want: we'll judge it on how close you get. It must be accessible and hold up on a phone. challenges.title: Product card grid
challenges.brief: Oak and Clay wants a new-arrivals section for the homepage. Shoppers should be able to scan the latest pieces quickly, see what each costs, and spot the bargains, with an easy way to see the whole range. Product details are supplied, and the reference design is the exact target, so match it as faithfully as you can. Keep it warm and uncluttered, like the shop itself, and make it hold up on smaller screens. Done means a shopper finds something they like and knows its price without hunting.
